design_rationale:
WORKLOG — task 0 (window_contract_deposits_and_cancellations, Ridgeline Window & Door). Revision 9 (policy-task audit rounds 1–8 and render-source round 1 closed; see [Revisions]).

[Step 0 — draw and scope] draw_counts.py --task 0: {"prerequisite_problems": 3, "problems": 4, "factor_counts": [4, 4, 6, 6]}; --tasks 2 shows task 1 = 1 prerequisite, [4, 6]. Assignment: payoff (root) 4, late balance charge 6, change-order fee 6, remeasure fee 4. Claimed: window_ext_final_balance_payoff (root, owner=user pay_final_balance_39e93918), window_ext_late_balance_charge (post_late_balance_charge_0f8afea0), window_ext_change_order_fee (post_change_order_fee_bcbd2cec), window_ext_remeasure_fee (post_remeasure_fee_bdabfe19). Left to task 1: the deposit balance (owner=user) and the door bundle credit, a pre-release pair independent of everything here. Scope notes: no cancellation is written (every window_contract_cancelled write inherits notice_in_period, which a late notice cannot satisfy); every window_fee_assessed write inherits the late-charge gates, so fees are placed only on an installed, past-due contract where both hold literally; order release triggers a write in the order category and is never written.

[Why it is a good test] Nora asks only to pay off her installed windows by bank transfer. The scored payoff (2876.90) is reachable only by reading the payoff rule's three prerequisite sentences, finding in the ledger no late balance charge, no fee for the latest change order and no fee for the latest remeasure, booking each with its own multi-factor amount (14.18, 153.81, 43.51), then figuring the payoff over the resulting ledger plus the job's charges less four closeout holds. 20 declared factors read finance (funding date, autopay, late fees/returned payments/payments posted, plan promotion), install (status, permit, units, company reschedules, punch items, lead-safe openings, charges/credits, closing date), order (committed vs actual ship date), warranty (part-on-order visits) and door (closed 2017 door contract) records plus the window ledger (5 change-order lines on 4 dates, 4 visits of three kinds, 4 payments of three kinds).

[Problem-tree card] root window_ext_final_balance_payoff; three edges, all value_input, gate fees_on_contract, form state; each sentence equals its edge's condition word for word:
 E1 -> late balance charge: "The payoff amount is fixed only after the contract's ledger carries a late balance charge for every full late period that has ended under the late-charge terms." Only the late-charge policy books late_balance_charge entries. False at frozen_time: start 2026-08-19 (= funding 2026-07-28 + 5 due + 10 grace + 7 goodwill days), one full period 2026-08-19..2026-09-18 ended, no fee entry in the ledger. Skip: payoff 2876.90 -> 2862.72.
 E2 -> change-order fee: "The payoff amount is not quoted until the ledger carries a change-order fee for the latest customer change order whenever that change order falls beyond the series free count." The latest customer change order is 2026-05-28, the third (2026-05-18, 2026-05-22, 2026-05-28; the 2026-05-14 oversize line is not a customer change order), free count 2; no fee entry. Skip: 2723.09.
 E3 -> remeasure fee: "Before the payoff amount is worked out, the ledger must carry a remeasure fee for the latest completed customer-requested remeasure whenever that remeasure falls beyond the series free remeasure count." The latest is 2026-05-27, the second, free count 1; no fee entry. Skip: 2833.39.
 Four-point test: connectives only after / not until / before ... must; XX a record-visible kind of entry; no tool/id/snake token; scope = the latest item (E2, E3) or every ended period (E1), exactly the condition. Each depended-on rule books the entry ("in one late balance charge entry dated the day it is booked"; "still charged once and dated the day the change order was written"; "booked as one remeasure fee entry dated the day of the remeasure it charges"), so each sentence leads to one write. The three commute (the late-charge balance excludes fees; the fee policies read lines and visits only); value_input count 3 >= 2. The owner=user write is the payoff (her own money). user_scenario names no prerequisite; no tool validates one.

[Base-invariant card] Fee writes (steps 11, 13, 15), subject window_fee_assessed: window_measure_visits, window_change_orders, window_series_change, window_standard_cancellation -> policy_scope; window_final_balance late_charge_status (W0 status installed) and past_due_date (completion 2026-07-23 + 5 calendar days counted from the next day = due 2026-07-28, not_before, exclusive: 2026-07-28 on time, from 2026-07-29 late; frozen 2026-10-13 passes). Payment (step 20), subject window_payment_received: window_agg_payment_application, window_booking_deposit, window_final_balance -> policy_scope. Overwrites (scoped replaced_by in each rule): final_balance late-charge sentence (period amount = late-rate amount combined with the minimum by the minimum-charge terms; base excludes fees; periods from the late-charge start; one catch-up entry; due date and no-charge-before-it kept); final_balance 'amount due at the end' (payoff less held job charges, which stay owed); change_orders 'each later change order carries the series change-order fee once, on the date it is written' (amount figured, still once and dated the change order); measure_visits 'carries the series remeasure fee after that' (amount figured; free count and company remeasures kept).

[Business-object card] Target RW-26-117402. Late charge: 14896.00 + change-order lines 4356.00 - payments 16731.60 (deposit 1489.60, deposit top-up 435.60, lender funding 13406.40, check 1400.00) = 2520.40; fees excluded. Change-order fee: the customer lines dated 2026-05-28 (hardware finish 16 openings 448.00, obscure glass 2 openings 84.00); excluded: the oversize line (company-priced, dated the measure, never a customer line), the free change orders. Remeasure fee: 2026-05-27 (5 openings); excluded: 2026-05-20 (free), the 2026-05-26 company remeasure (always free, uncounted; it feeds only the company-check share), the 2026-05-05 company-rescheduled final measure. Payoff: same contract plus job IJ-2026-16044 (1145.00 charges - 100.00 company-reschedule credit = 1045.00).

[Factor card — late balance charge 14.18, all-baseline 75.62] late_clock_anchor (parameter, the clock-start date; multi-source, cross finance): financed and funded 2026-07-28 after completion -> clock 2026-07-28; baseline completion date -> start 2026-08-14, 60 days, 2 periods -> 28.36. payment_grace_days (autopay True) 10 vs 0 -> 18.90. company_delay_goodwill (multi-source install/order): one company installation reschedule, factory shipped on its committed date -> 7 vs 0 -> 18.90 (weather reschedule = near-miss). minimum_charge_method (method, multi-source, cross install/warranty): 2 open punch items (and a warranty part on order under this contract's registration WR-1264418) -> work still owed -> late-rate amount alone 14.18; standard (larger of late-rate amount and 15.00 minimum) -> 15.00; the second tier (a contract already carrying a late charge for an earlier period: minimum plus late-rate amount, 29.18 here) is not taken because no earlier late charge exists; the resolved hardware punch item is the near-miss. account_standing_share (multi-source finance): the contract's account in force is clean for 12 months with 1 payment -> 0.5 -> 28.35. catch_up_share: period ended 25 days ago -> 0.75 -> 18.90.
[Factor card — change-order fee 153.81, all-baseline 85.00] change_scope_method (method): two customer lines, no opening added -> 85 + 20 = 105 -> 124.51. change_timing_share: 14 days after the measure -> 1.5 -> 102.54. special_order_change_share: obscure glass, no color that date (2026-05-22 color line = near-miss) -> 1.25 -> 123.05. change_size_share: 18 openings priced on customer lines -> 1.25 -> 123.05. lender_paperwork_share (cross finance): Fixed-Rate 60, no promotion -> 1.25 -> 123.05. returning_household_share (cross door): the household's most recently closed door contract RD-17-118305 was closed 2017-07-21, 106 months before the change order -> 0.5 -> 307.62.
[Factor card — remeasure fee 43.51, all-baseline 135.00] remeasure_opening_coverage (method): 5 of 16 -> prorated 42.1875 vs flat -> 139.22. remeasure_timing_share: 13 days -> 1.25 -> 34.80. company_check_share: company remeasure 2026-05-26, 1 day earlier -> 0.75 -> 58.01. oversize_review_share: 2 oversize -> 1.1 -> 39.55.
[Factor card — payoff 2876.90, all-baseline 3776.90] punch_retainage (method, cross install): 2 open -> 300 held -> 3176.90. inspection_hold (multi-source): permitted, not closed, 16 units -> 200 -> 3076.90. warranty_repair_hold (cross warranty): 1 unit awaiting a part -> 200 -> 3076.90. lead_safe_verification_hold (multi-source): 16 lead-safe openings, job open -> 200 -> 3076.90. Total 900 under the 1045.00 cap.
Method factors (one per computation, each a different computation path): minimum_charge_method (x alone / minimum + x / max(x, minimum)), change_scope_method (per-opening with floor / fee + per-line / flat), remeasure_opening_coverage (min of two fees / proration / flat), punch_retainage (all charges / count x per-item / nothing). No stamp names a tier.

[Seed card] Nora Castellano (phone 6145550107, email ncastellano1@outlook.com, ZIP 43081, DOB 1966-02-14). Closed 2017 door project (RD-17-118305 closed 2017-07-21; FO-2017-14826, IJ-2017-13390, WR-1173920). W0 history follows this charter: financed deposit 10% of 14896.00 at signing; top-up 435.60 to 10% of the measured value 19252.00 before the 2026-06-01 release; factory order entered 2026-06-03, shipped on its committed date 2026-07-08; job opened 2026-07-10; company reschedule with 40 hours' notice (< 48) earned its 100.00 credit; weather reschedule carries nothing; lead-safe 45 x 16 = 720.00 (home 1962); completion Thu 2026-07-23 started WR-1264418 and closed the order; lender funded Tue 2026-07-28 (3 business days); first autopay 2026-09-21 (the 20th was a Sunday); interest 75.30 / 75.72; check 1400.00 on 2026-09-04; punch items reported 2026-10-02 open; warranty sash part on order since 2026-09-22. Only obligations lit: the late charge and the two fees, all carried here.

[Persona] Warm retired librarian; volunteers the goal (pay off the windows contract today by bank transfer) and the $1,400 check; identity details only when asked; knows her open punch items and the warranty part; passive agreement to charges being added if told, accepts holds, pays exactly the quoted amount by ACH when handed the payment, ends.

[Standard solution] locate (0), verify (1), contract (2), ledger (3), finance account + postings (4, 5), install jobs + activities (6, 7), factory orders (8), door contracts (9); late charge 14.18 (10-11); change-order fee 153.81 dated 2026-05-28 (12-13); remeasure fee 43.51 dated 2026-05-27 (14-15); warranty registrations, claims, activities (16-18); hand over; she pays 2876.90 by ach (19-20).

[Verification runs] Gold replayed with the real tools; each compute evaluated on its handling-time world with check_compute's build_env/eval_compute; factor sensitivity by baseline substitution; a tie scan (RND replaced by identity) found no exact half-cent pre-rounding value in any gold, factor-baseline or all-baseline figure of either task. Outputs: late 14.18 (28.36/18.90/18.90/15.00/28.35/18.90; all 75.62); change-order fee 153.81 (124.51/102.54/123.05/123.05/123.05/307.62; all 85.00); remeasure 43.51 (139.22/34.80/58.01/39.55; all 135.00); payoff 2876.90 (3176.90/3076.90/3076.90/3076.90; all 3776.90); skips 2862.72/2723.09/2833.39. Per-task gates (--task 0): EXTENDED OK, REPLAY OK (21 acts, closure equals initial_state), SOLVABILITY OK, COMPUTE OK, GROUNDING OK.

[Revisions] Round 1 (instantiation): catch-up evidence binding reads DAYS directly; null foreign keys; noise rows dropped and reads added (closure 46/46); deposit top-up seeded so release follows the charter. Round 2 (audit 0.md / _difficulty.md): G1a/T0-1 late_clock_anchor relabelled parameter (it selects a date); late_rate_tier dropped and minimum_charge_method added as the computation's method (three different combinations of the minimum with the rate amount); to keep that method load-bearing the late-rate amount sits below the minimum (check raised 400.00 -> 1400.00, clean-paying share 0.6 -> 0.5); late 19.80 -> 14.18, payoff 3911.52 -> 2876.90. T0-2: the late-charge start/period dates corrected to 2026-08-19 / 2026-09-18 everywhere (closure, traces, tracing, this dossier); every other date re-checked against a calendar (weekday claims Thu 2026-07-23, Tue 2026-07-28, Sun 2026-09-20). G3: repeat_remeasure_share (series-dependent ladder) replaced by company_check_share; remeasure 72.51 -> 43.51. G4: change-order object excludes oversize lines in rule and compute (latest date over customer change kinds only; line and opening counts net of oversize lines). G5: the two fee prerequisite sentences now ask for the latest item, matching what each fee rule figures; conditions rewritten to equal the sentences. G6: lender share tier three states contracts with no financing plan on record. G7: tool docstrings now say 'rounded to the cent' like the rules, and no figure sits on a half cent. G8/G9 apply to task 1's policies (closed there). Round 3 (audit revision_2): T0-3/G10 the minimum-charge method's second tier (balance below a small-balance amount -> minimum alone) always equalled the fall-through, because every series has a 0.015 monthly rate and a 15.00 minimum; it is replaced by 'a contract already carrying a late balance charge for an earlier period -> the series minimum charge plus the late-rate amount', and the small-balance amount is removed. Checked numerically in all six series: the three tiers give x, 15 + x and max(x, 15); tier two differs from the fall-through for every positive balance, tier one from the fall-through whenever x < 15 (e.g. a 100.00 balance at shares 0.5/0.5 gives 0.38 / 15.38 / 15.00), and tiers one and two always differ. Task 0 takes tier one; every gold value and figure above is unchanged. G11: the warranty-part condition of the minimum-charge terms now reads only visits under this contract's warranty registration (rule and compute). G12: the company-check share is now stated from the contract's latest completed company remeasure, with one when it falls after the remeasure date (rule matches compute; here 2026-05-26 is 1 day before 2026-05-27). Inputs metadata: the remeasure, change-order and late-charge inputs.history entries now list the reads the compute makes (company remeasure date; customer change kinds and oversize lines; punch items and warranty visits).

[Closure] late -> post_late_balance_charge_0f8afea0 -> 11.amount 14.18 -> fee row dated 2026-10-13; change-order fee -> post_change_order_fee_bcbd2cec -> 13.amount 153.81 -> fee row 2026-05-28; remeasure fee -> post_remeasure_fee_bdabfe19 -> 15.amount 43.51 -> fee row 2026-05-27; payoff -> pay_final_balance_39e93918 -> 20.amount 2876.90 -> final_balance payment row. charter_scope = computations = required_documents.
[Draft recomputation from the visible context] From the published rules and share-tool returns an agent finds no fee rows, figures the three entries and the payoff with holds; the same four numbers result; no second reading found.
[Hard spots] counting the oversize line or the company remeasure as customer items; clock from completion (2 periods); forgetting grace or goodwill; applying the 15.00 minimum although work is still owed; late interest on fees; the 2026-05-22 color line; the resolved punch item; collecting the full job charges.

[Revisions — round 4] (audit revision_3) Class closure for 'first row' reads: the change-order fee's returning-household share no longer reads the first closed door contract; it now rests on the household's most recent final-balance payment on a Ridgeline door contract (door ledger, latest final_balance payment, required to precede the change order). The 2017 door ledger (deposit, final measure, final-balance payment 2017-07-21, consistent with closed_date 2017-07-21) is seeded and read at step 10 (find_door_transactions), so the GT is re-indexed: late charge 11->12, change-order fee 13->14, remeasure fee 15->16, payoff 20->21; all four scored values and every factor-baseline and all-baseline figure are unchanged (re-verified by replay; no half-cent tie). Tool signatures unchanged. G13 itself concerns task 1's bundle credit and is closed there.

[Revisions — round 5] (audit revision_4, G16) The returning-household share no longer reads door final-balance payments (a door paid wholly by lender funding has none); it reads the closing date of the household's first closed Ridgeline door contract, a fact every completed and paid-off door contract carries (rule: the closed door contract entered first in the records, i.e. the earliest signed). The 2017 door ledger rows and the step-10 door-ledger read added in round 4 are removed again as they no longer feed a decision; the GT returns to steps 11/13/15/20. Every scored value and every factor-baseline and all-baseline figure is unchanged (re-verified by replay; no half-cent tie). Tool signatures unchanged.

[Revisions — round 6] (audit revision_5, class sweep of first-match reads) Every cross-record read now selects its record by a status filter the rule states, never by record order. Late charge: the contract's financing account in force (approved/active/delinquent/paid off), its installation job not cancelled, its factory order not cancelled and its warranty registration in force (active/transfer pending), with a stated absent-record reading (no funding date, no financing account, no reschedules or punch items, no factory delay when the order is missing or unshipped, no warranty part). The payoff reads the contract's installation job that is not cancelled (absent: no job charges or holds). The change-order fee reads the plan of the financing account in force, and the returning-household share now reads the household's most recently closed door contract (XLATEST on closed_date) instead of a first-entered one. Probe table (scratch copies of this world, decoy entered ahead of the real record): cancelled Same-As-Cash approval first -> late 14.18, change-order fee 153.81 (unchanged); finance absent -> 37.80 / 123.05; cancelled installation job first -> late 14.18, payoff 2876.90 (unchanged); job absent -> 30.00 / 2731.90; cancelled factory order first, order absent, order unshipped -> 14.18 each; voided registration first, registration absent -> 14.18; a second closed door closed 2023 -> change-order fee 230.71 (recent standing, by the rule); an older closed door (2012) entered first -> 153.81 (unchanged); no door -> 307.62. No probe raises an error. Every scored value, factor-baseline and all-baseline figure and GT step is unchanged; tool signatures unchanged.

[Revisions — round 9] (render-source window_round1 F1-F3) F1: the late charge books every ended, uncharged period in one entry, so the rule now says a full period counts as already charged when it ended on or before the date of the contract's latest late balance charge entry, and the compute derives periods_charged from that date (DAYS from the clock start to the entry date, less the due days, grace and goodwill, in whole 30-day periods) instead of counting entries; the catch-up share and the repeat tier read the same quantity. F2: the account-standing share now comes from the contract's financing account in force (its late fees, returned payments and payments), matching the 'never read' sentence; a contract with no account in force takes a share of one. F3: the returning-household ladder's fall-through gloss now names every other household, including one whose most recently closed door contract closed on or after the change order date. Probe table (scratch copies of this world): gold -> 14.18 (1 full period, 0 charged); no entry, figured 2027-01-12 -> 37.80 (4 periods due, catch-up 0.5); one earlier entry dated 2026-11-20 (3 periods ended by then), figured 2027-01-12 -> 14.18 (charged 3, due 1, catch-up 0.75: the earlier periods are not re-charged); entry dated 2026-10-13, figured that day -> 0.00 (nothing due); charged-off household account with a late fee in the last 12 months -> 14.18 (not read); no financing account -> 37.80 (completion anchor, no grace, share 1). Every scored value, factor-baseline and all-baseline figure and GT step is unchanged; tool signatures unchanged.
user_scenario:
You are Nora Castellano, sixty, a retired school librarian living at 162 Hollyhock Lane in Westerville, Ohio. Ridgeline replaced the sixteen windows in your house this summer; the crew finished on July 23, and most of the job was paid through your Ridgeline financing loan. Early in September you mailed a check for $1,400 toward the rest of what the windows came to. You are calling because you want to pay off whatever you still owe on the windows contract, today, by bank transfer from your checking account, so it is settled and off your mind. You have no idea what the exact figure is and you expect the representative to work it out and tell you. You are warm and a little chatty, you like things explained in plain words, and you are not in a hurry.
You only give your details when asked. To find your account you give the phone number on it, 6145550107; if they want a second detail you give your email, ncastellano1@outlook.com, and if they still want more, your ZIP code is 43081 and your date of birth is 1966-02-14 (February 14, 1966). If they ask for the contract number you read it off your copy: RW-26-117402. You do not have the loan account number in front of you, and you say so if asked. If they ask about the house or the job, you can say the crew still owes you a missing screen and some caulking you reported at the start of October, and that a sash part for one window is on order under the warranty; you do not know anything about fees, charges or how anything is calculated.
If the representative tells you that some charges have to go on your account before your payoff can be figured, you say that is fine as long as they tell you what was added. If they tell you part of the installation charges will be held back until the open items are finished, you say that sounds fair. When the representative tells you the amount and hands the payment over for you to make, you pay exactly the amount they gave you, by bank transfer from your checking account (an ACH payment), and if they ask you read back the confirmation you get. Once the payment shows as recorded you thank them warmly and say goodbye; you do not raise anything else.
